_comment: Guided tour of the native converter. 'name' is the emtk control (a spec action, or the history table). The Qt tool keeps guide.json.

steps.title: The drop decides the direction
steps.text: There is no pack/unpack switch. Drop a vendor file (.ptu, .spc, .ht3) and it is packed into a .pto. Drop a .pto and it is unpacked back out to the vendor files and results it holds. The tool reads the suffix and goes. Every conversion becomes a row of this table.

steps.title: Nothing is ever deleted
steps.text: Packing writes the .pto beside the vendor file and keeps the original, then checks the container against its checksum. Unpacking writes the vendor files back and keeps the container. Either direction can be repeated or thrown away with no loss. Add files... does what a drop does, with a dialog.

await.hint: Press Add files..., then pick a file or close the dialog.

steps.title: Files dropped together are one measurement
steps.text: A recording split across m000.spc, m001.spc, ... is one measurement, so files dropped together (or chosen together) are packed into one .pto, in file-name order. The row lists them in that order.

steps.title: The .set rides along, never leads
steps.text: A Becker & Hickl .set is an .spc's sidecar. Next to its .spc it is picked up automatically with the file it belongs to; offered alone it is Rejected: it is not a measurement, it is the header of one.

steps.title: Tidy up
steps.text: Clear history removes the finished rows from the list. It never touches a file on disk.
